description:
Surfaced by the cold review of fz-5xp.3.

fz-5xp.3 made the calling convention a DECLARED property: `extern "fz"` means the
symbol receives `*mut Process`. Three primitives were converted. Seven more take
the process in their Rust bodies but still declare `extern "C"`:

    fz_panic, fz_self, fz_send, fz_spawn, fz_spawn_opt, fz_make_ref,
    fz_make_resource       (src/modules/runtime_library/kernel.fz)

They work only because BOTH doors still intercept them by name before the extern
lane is reached. So the declaration is now a provably wrong fact sitting in what
fz-5xp.3 made the source of truth, and `.agent/docs/externs.md` tells the reader
there is "no lowering function to write and no interpreter match arm to add" --
which is exactly the machinery these seven still depend on.

Same shape for the four `fz_op_*_bb` comparisons, whose declared `binary` params
never become `*const u8`.

WHY THEY WERE NOT CONVERTED. The fz-5xp.3 design comment splits the if-chain into
(a) "needs the process" and (b) "is an intrinsic": the lowering emits something
other than a call. These seven are all (b) -- `fz_send` retargets to
`fz_send_ref`, `fz_spawn` wraps a closure, `fz_make_ref` calls a differently
named raw symbol, `fz_panic` diverges. Folding them into the ABI would conflate
two invariants, so fz-5xp.3 correctly left them alone.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING is the third category the ABI cannot express. An
intrinsic is not an extern: it names no callable symbol and honours no wire
type. Until the surface can say so, an intrinsic must wear a lie.

This is the same conclusion fz-5xp.29 reaches from the other direction (its
declarations name symbols nothing backs). Do them together: one `intrinsic`
declaration form makes both problems melt, and lets the generic extern path
refuse an intrinsic outright instead of silently mis-marshalling one.

Related: fz-5xp.29, fz-5xp.3, fz-5xp.21.
title: Seven process-taking primitives are still declared extern "C"
